| [ADR-068](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-068.md) v2 | Reading and filing follow a written protocol: its invariants are held in this decision, and its steps in a skill that changes with practice | The record takes in reading through a practice of eleven steps: intake, a check against the record, identifiers, registration, a lawful copy, reading, verification, filing the reading, filing the argument, accounting for everything, and acknowledgement. | [ADR-075](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-075.md) v4 | A synthesis in a filed source is audited and, when it integrates, filed as a thesis claim with its components mapped, rather than mapped to its source turns and left | Filing has treated a source's syntheses (executive summaries, positive accounts, recaps, "refreshed syntheses") as recaps: each item is mapped to the turn it came from, and the synthesis is left. That finds new content but leaves the integration with no address. So the record can't say what its current account is, and later syntheses can't be checked for drift. The exchange "Individuation, Possibility, and Disposition" produced four summaries of the record's account. They recast the owner's prompts as the argument's own logic and dropped two of the owner's contributions, and nothing on the record could catch it. This decision adds a synthesis audit to the read-and-file skill: find every synthesis, group its versions, classify it as descriptive, supposed or proposed, map its components to codes, and check attribution, coverage, fidelity, standing and integration. The latest version of each distinct proposed or supposed thesis is filed as one CLAIM, with its components in `rests_on` or the body, and revised in place when it returns. A synthesis is admitted as an independent hypothesis, a derived result or an explanatory integration, each with its own test (versions 2 and 3). Rejected: a new scheme for positions, until a synthesis CLAIM strains; filing every version; and the status quo. | Proposed — Amended by [ADR-084](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-084.md): a SYNTHESIS is an account, and whatever adds to its components is a CLAIM. Steps 1 to 4 apply to accounts and to a source's syntheses as before; step 5's admission routes are now the test a claim whose premises are claims passes to show it has content of its own, filed under [ADR-072](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-072.md)'s rule. |
| [ADR-078](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-078.md) | The record is reviewed periodically for synthesis opportunities: CLAIMs that are syntheses filed as claims are moved into the SYNTHESIS scheme, and integrations whose parts the record holds are filed when they pass admission | [ADR-075](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-075.md) audits the syntheses a source brings, and [ADR-076](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-076.md) gives them a scheme and a current-account view. Neither looks at what the record already holds. Some CLAIMs are syntheses filed before the scheme existed, [CLAIM-545](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-545.md) among them. Some integrations sit in the record as parts, such as `complements` clusters, questions with several answers and deep chains, that no entry states. This decision adds a periodic synthesis review, carried by the `synthesis-review` skill. Its first stage is mechanical: scratch/formal/synthesis_candidates.py ranks candidates in two arms, migration and opportunity, and decides nothing. A reviewer then shortlists a dozen at most, preferring in-force components and lines the current-account view does not cover. Each is audited with [ADR-075](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-075.md)'s five checks and admitted by one of its three routes or not at all. An admitted migration moves into the scheme, with its relations audited. An admitted opportunity is filed as a Proposed SYNTHESIS in the assistant's voice. Nothing is set Current, and what is not admitted is recorded with its reason. Rejected: reviewing only at filing time; filing every candidate the ranking finds; leaving the sweep ad hoc. | Proposed — Amended by ADR-084: the review's arms are now coverage of each scope by an account, claims that only map their components (Arm A), and integrations held in parts, filed as claims when they pass ADR-075's test (Arm B); the synthesis-review skill carries them. |
| [ADR-079](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-079.md) | Each directed relation is stored on one side only, the side a filer writes, and its converse is derived when the record is read; the sweep that removes the stored converses is this decision's demonstration | Every directed relation in the record was stored twice, once on each end, and `luria link --fix` kept the second copy in step. About 2,770 values in 1,260 entries were such copies. Adding a relation to a new scheme, as the SYNTHESIS scheme needed, meant widening the stored converse on every target scheme. luria 1.10.0, which CI pins, can mark one side of a pair `derived`: only the other side is written, readers compute the converse, and `luria repair` moves anything written on the derived side to the primary side of the other entry. This decision marks the derived side of every directed pair, 32 field declarations, choosing the side the config's own blurbs already describe as written by `luria link --fix`. Symmetric relations (`complements`, `rivals`, `compared_against`) stay as they are, since luria never derives them. Rejected: keeping both sides; choosing the derived side pair by pair on a different principle; a partial switch. | Proposed |
| [ADR-081](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-081.md) | The Pages site deploys at most once every two hours: a merge still triggers it, a gate skips the build when the last deploy is under two hours old or already published the commit, and a scheduled run every two hours publishes what the gate skipped | Every Docs run on main triggered a full Pages build, and the build takes a long time. Merges come in runs, so most builds were superseded before they finished. A gate job now reads the last deploy to the `github-pages` environment. It skips the build when that deploy is under two hours old, or when it already published the commit; a manual run always builds. A scheduled run every two hours applies the same gate, so a skipped merge is published by the next one, at most about two hours late. Rejected: a schedule alone, which drops publish-on-merge; a concurrency group alone, which still builds after every merge; and counting the workflow's own runs, which would count the runs the gate skipped. | Proposed |
| [ADR-082](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-082.md) v2 | The nucleating-argument line is split in three: nucleating-argument keeps how an argument drifts, anchors and pays for anchoring; what a record of inquiry keeps and the record as its own apparatus become lines of their own, because their parts barely relate to the rest | The nucleating-argument line's first account ([ADR-083](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-083.md)) fell into five parts. | [ADR-083](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-083.md) v3 | An account the record holds only in parts, for a line or a part of one, gets a SYNTHESIS that restates it, so the account has an address: it adds nothing, and its standing is its components'; there is one account per scope, an account may integrate the accounts of its parts, and a line whose parts barely relate is a candidate to split | [ADR-075](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-075.md) began from a filing gap: an integration left with no address, so the record could not say what its current account is, nor check a later synthesis for drift. The admission test it added guards against importing a source's broad summary as one more claim. [ADR-078](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-078.md)'s review reused that test to backfill the current-account view. There the common verdict was that a candidate's integration was already stated in its components' bodies and notes, and nothing was filed. That recreates the original gap: the nucleating-argument line has an account, scattered, and the view shows none. This decision gives such an account a SYNTHESIS (version 3: the scheme is now accounts only, ADR-084). It restates a line's account as the record holds it, maps every component, and adds nothing; its standing is its components', and the view sets it out under its line. The review files one when a candidate fails the claim test only because the record already holds its integration, and never when it fails on a free parameter, an error or a contradiction. There is one account per scope, a line or a part of one, not one per line, and a line's account may integrate its parts' accounts. When a line's parts barely relate, that is a signal to split the line, which is decided separately. The demonstration is the former nucleating-argument line: its account, split into part syntheses and a line synthesis over them, after the split of the line (ADR-082). Rejected: treating lines without a synthesis as findings only; admitting such accounts; a separate scheme. | Proposed |
| [ADR-084](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-084.md) | A SYNTHESIS is an account of a scope of the record's argument and asserts nothing of its own, and whatever adds to its components is a CLAIM: the admitted syntheses return to the claims they were, the admission test becomes the test for filing a claim whose premises are claims, and a claim's premises are claims again | [ADR-076](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-076.md) gave syntheses a scheme. An entry earned a place in it by passing one of [ADR-075](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-075.md)'s admission routes. Asked what the admitted syntheses add, the record's answer was one proposition each, with a credence, a voice, a warrant and a defeater. Those are a CLAIM's fields. The owner observed that such an addition should be a claim, which is atomic however many premises it has. The owner also observed that the unadmitted accounts, which map a scope's components and add nothing, are what "synthesis" means. This decision makes SYNTHESIS the scheme of accounts only. Its status is whether the mapping is right. Its defeater is fidelity. It has no role, warrant, route or premises. Anything that adds to its components is a CLAIM, filed under [ADR-072](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-072.md)'s rule. [ADR-075](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-075.md)'s routes become the way such a claim shows it has content of its own. The nine claims moved into the scheme are restored under their own codes, and the two syntheses that were never claims become new claims. A claim's `rests_on` names claims only again, so the patches [ADR-077](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-077.md) and [ADR-080](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-080.md) made are undone. It supersedes [ADR-076](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-076.md), [ADR-077](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-077.md) and [ADR-080](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-080.md), and amends [ADR-075](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-075.md), [ADR-078](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-078.md) and [ADR-083](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-083.md). Rejected: a field telling the two kinds apart within one scheme; the status quo; moving the integrations to new claim codes; an `integrates` field on CLAIM; making accounts generated views. | Proposed |
| [ADR-085](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-085.md) v2 | An entry carries every line whose argument it takes part in: the first line of each entry it answers, objects to or bears on, and of each question it refines, in one step; resting on or using an entry of another line is a dependency across lines, not participation, and stays a reported crossing | `line` takes several values, and a line is "a named line of the record's own argument, so that a line can be set aside as a whole and what depends on it can be found" ([ADR-032](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-032.md)). Nothing said when an entry should carry a second line. [ADR-082](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-082.md) answered it for one case, the split of nucleating-argument: a moved entry keeps the old line when it answers, refines or objects to one of that line's entries. This decision makes the rule general and adds `bears_on`: an entry carries the first line of each entry it answers, objects to or bears on, and of each question it refines (version 2). A line the target carries second does not pass, and nothing cascades, so one pass is final. Resting on or using one does not count; that is a dependency the `argument` chain reports as a crossing, which is what [ADR-032](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-032.md) meant it to do. Neither does `complements` alone. The demonstration gives the line to the eleven entries among the lint's 79 cross-line steps that bear on a question of the premise's line. Version 2's sweep applies it record-wide. Rejected: counting `complements`; counting `rests_on`; every line a target carries; following the rule until nothing changes; leaving it to judgement entry by entry. | Proposed |
| [ADR-086](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-086.md) | An entry shows the accounts that integrate it: `integrates` gets a derived converse, `integrated_by`, on every scheme an account can integrate, so a part of a line's argument is visible from its members and not only from the current-account view | The synthesis reviews of 2026-11-10 divided lines into parts, each with an account, and kept some densely linked parts together in one line. The owner asked whether tags or some other abstraction express what such a cluster has in common. Measured, no `topics` tag both covers a part and is specific to it, because tags record what a work is about, at the grain of a field. Some parts hang from a root question or a hub claim, and six have none. The one thing that names every part is its account, and `integrates` runs one way: no entry shows which account it belongs to. This decision gives `integrates` a derived converse, `integrated_by`, declared on the seven schemes an account can integrate, and stored on no entry ([ADR-079](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-079.md)). On the record of 2026-11-10 it annotates 163 entries, 18 of them with two or more accounts. Rejected: cluster-level tags; a stored `part` field; leaving it to the current-account view. | Proposed |
| [ADR-087](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-087.md) | The readiness line is split in two: readiness keeps keeping a rare capability and reaching and paying for configurations under budgets; when transient support can be withdrawn becomes the line transient-support, because that part barely relates to the other two | The synthesis review of 2026-11-10 gave readiness its first account, over three parts: keeping and judging a rare capability, reaching and paying for configurations under budgets, and withdrawing transient support. | [ADR-089](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-089.md) | Normative judgment about organizations becomes a line of its own, organizational-normativity, split from will-organization: whether an organization's own dynamics ground norms, and what judging one needs, is a question of its own, while acting as one stays, because its root question refines the line's own | The synthesis review of 2026-11-11 gave will-organization its first account, over six parts.
